description: One recorded anchor run: a boss Health.Value time series plus the run manifest that says what was being measured. NOT AN EXTRACTED GAME TABLE. It is deliberately absent from core.tables.TABLE_NAMES, which is the registry tools/rmdata_extract seeds per build - adding the anchor there would create an empty anchor table inside every data/rmdata/<build>/tables/ directory, and core/tables.py is a FROZEN file besides. It reuses exactly one piece of the existing machinery: core.tables.validate_table, which takes a schema DICT and needs no registry. core.table_deep.deep_problems CANNOT gate it, because that function raises KeyError for any name outside TABLE_NAMES (core/table_deep.py:356-357); the falsification spec section D.4.1 claims both and is corrected here, pinned by tests/test_embargo.py. ROWS ARE SAMPLES, one per MainThreadTick, appended by the proposed GET /record/* endpoint. THE SAMPLE RATE IS 4 Hz AND IT IS A CEILING, NOT A KNOB: it is set by SampleEveryFrames = 15 (bridge/src/RedMoon.Bridge/Plugin.cs:41) at about 60 fps, and the falsification spec section C tolerances were computed against it. Raising it raises the ECS read rate for every consumer of that tick. A 4 Hz series therefore CANNOT isolate every hit - abilities with hits_per_cast up to 4 exist and several can land inside one 250 ms window - so the per-hit gate runs over ISOLATED deltas only: a health drop bracketed by at least one no-change sample on each side, containing exactly one ability application. THE MANIFEST IS A FIFTH ENVELOPE KEY beside table, build, schema_version and rows. That was REASONED and is now PROBED: validate_table requires those four and rejects undeclared fields on ROWS only, so an extra envelope key passes. Keeping the manifest in the same file as the series means a run cannot be separated from the statement of what it measured.

index.description: Monotonic sample index from the arm instant, starting at 0. Gaps are impossible by construction; a gap in captured_at with no gap here means the tick stalled, and the A.5 checklist discards a run with any gap over 3 tick intervals (about 750 ms) because such a series cannot be integrated.

captured_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 instant, from the envelope the bridge already stamps (BridgeServer.cs:536). The clock is validated once against reality by the single paired A2 run: the video timestamp of the death animation must agree with the sample at which health_value reaches 0 to within one sample interval.

prefab_guid.description: The queried boss PrefabGUID, RESTATED on every sample rather than written once in the manifest. Restating it is the control: a spawned boss carries the SAME PrefabGUID as its prefab and the two do not agree, and cycle 2 fixed the resulting count by deduping, which made the CHOICE order-dependent. A sample that restates a guid other than the queried one means the recorder followed a stale entity handle.

carries_prefab_marker.description: The liveness control, read the same way ComponentDumper.cs:557-561 already reads it. TRUE MEANS DISCARD THE RUN, not smooth it: the prefab reads Health.Value 0, so a recorder latched onto the prefab records a perfectly flat zero series that a naive reading turns into an instantaneous kill. This is the same control that caught the phase 1 generic reader. POST /record/start REQUIRES a match with this false and returns subject_not_spawned otherwise, which encodes the phase 3 timing trap as a precondition rather than a comment: the first phase 3 control found the prefab only at about 5 s of uptime and the instance by 20 s. Poll for the SUBJECT, never for ready:true.

health_value.description: ProjectM.Health.Value on the boss instance, via the typed accessor at ComponentDumper.cs:568-573. This is the falsifiable quantity: a per-sample delta attributable to one ability application is a number the game itself computed, with no human term in it, which is what a kill duration can never be.

health_max.description: ProjectM.Health.MaxHealth._Value on the INSTANCE, and the only place a time-to-kill denominator can come from. It is 0 on all 65 prefabs and 8107 on the live Dracula instance, measured, and 0 to 8107 is not a ratio so there is no spawn-scaling factor to recover. UNVERIFIED and it matters: under what difficulty was 8107 measured, given Brutal multiplies V Blood MaxHealthModifier by 1.25. UNVERIFIED at n=1: whether it is stable across two spawns of the same boss.

is_dead.description: ProjectM.Health.IsDead. A terminal sample is health_value <= 0 OR this true, and the OR is not laziness: HealthConstants.DestroyOnDeath and DestroyAfterDuration exist, so the entity may vanish before a zero sample lands. The recorder treats a subject that disappears from the world as a terminal event rather than an error.

player_health_value.description: ProjectM.Health.Value on the player character, from the SAME tick (StateReader.cs:407-418). Free, and it is the entire basis of the EHP gate. Omitted when the character entity could not be resolved on that tick, never zeroed - a zero player health is a real and different statement.

player_health_max.description: Player max health from the same tick. Omitted rather than zeroed on a failed resolve.

blood_quality.description: Live blood quality (StateReader.cs:440-441), restated per sample because it decays during a fight. The B.2 matching rule compares runs on this to within one 10-point bucket, so a run whose quality crosses a bucket boundary mid-fight is a fact the manifest alone would hide.

blood_type.description: Live blood type name, joining tables/blood_types.json (13 rows). NAMES ONLY: every magnitude is scaled from blood quality at runtime and none are on the prefab, so the blood contribution is DECLARED AND OMITTED from computation until magnitudes are sourced live.

note.description: Free-text operator note attached to one sample. NEVER PARSED. It exists so a phase change or a mistake can be recorded at the instant it happened rather than reconstructed afterwards.
